title: Cesium Chloride Gradients
author: Matthew Sullivan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.c7dzi5
materials: With sterile pipet tip, remove 100µl. undetermined

steps.title: Prepare filtered seawater
steps.instruction: Filter seawater through a 0.02 µm (or 0.2 µm) filter and autoclave the filtrate.

steps.title: Make CsCl density solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve CsCl in the autoclaved seawater to obtain four solutions: p1.2 (11.19 g per 50 ml), p1.4 (26.94 g per 50 ml), p1.5 (33.74 g per 50 ml) and p1.65 (43.78 g per 50 ml). Verify each by removing 1 ml with a sterile pipette tip, weighing it on a balance, and confirming that the weight equals the target density (e.g., 1 ml of p1.2 should weigh 1.2 g). Adjust CsCl amount if needed.

steps.title: Layer CsCl gradient
steps.instruction: Using thin‑walled SW40 or SW28 tubes, layer the prepared CsCl solutions from the bottom upward. Either use a gradient fractionator (e.g., Labconco) or carefully dispense with Pasteur pipettes. Volumes per rotor:

substeps.instruction: SW40 rotor: 2 ml p1.65, 3 ml p1.5, 3 ml p1.4, 1 ml p1.2.
SW28 rotor: 5 ml p1.65, 8 ml p1.5, 9 ml p1.4, 3 ml p1.65 (as written; the p1.2 layer is intended to equilibrate the sample before it reaches the p1.4 layer).

steps.title: Add sample to gradient
steps.instruction: Carefully layer the sample on top of the gradient: up to ~5 ml for SW40 tubes or up to ~15 ml for SW28 tubes. This can be done with a fraction collector or with Pasteur pipettes.

steps.title: Centrifuge gradient
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a Beckman SW40 or SW28 rotor and centrifuge at 24 000 rpm for 4 h at 4 °C. If using a Beckman SW‑48 swinging‑bucket rotor, set deceleration to 9 to reduce mixing of the gradient.

steps.title: Prepare collection tubes
steps.instruction: Label sterile 0.5 ml tubes (for SW40) or 1.5 ml tubes (for SW28) with numbers 1–24. Open the tubes in a rack and place each on a ring stand.

steps.title: Puncture gradient tube
steps.instruction: Using a sterile 20‑gauge needle (bevel up), puncture the side of the centrifuged gradient tube about 2 mm from the bottom. Optionally remove the top sample layer with a pipette, as it contains no virus after centrifugation.

steps.title: Collect gradient fractions
steps.instruction: Allow droplets to flow from the puncture point and collect them sequentially into the labeled tubes, filling each tube in order. Do not collect the bottom layer, which does not contain virus.

steps.title: Measure fraction density
steps.instruction: Place each collection tube on a 4‑place balance fitted in a holder (make a holder by cutting off the top 1 in of a 15 ml tube with the cap on). Record the weight. Then:

substeps.instruction: Remove 100 µl of the fraction, weigh the tube again, record the value, and return the 100 µl to the tube.
Repeat the 100 µl removal, weighing, and return once more (total of three measurements per tube).
Calculate the average of the three weight values for each tube and multiply the average by 10; the result equals the CsCl density of that fraction.

steps.title: Pool virus‑containing fractions
steps.instruction: Select fractions whose calculated densities fall between p1.4 and p1.5, pool them, and proceed to DNA extraction or, alternatively, confirm virus presence by staining 10 µl of the pooled sample with SYBR Gold.
